A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures and tables, support reliable comparison; no essential material remains unreadable.

before.justification: V2 reports original results from 94 participants providing 470 evaluations of 90 PrivacyLens scenarios, alongside five proxy LLMs, with quantitative comparisons and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: V4 retains the original participant and proxy-LLM results, including agreement, correlation, semantic-similarity measurements, and qualitative findings.

M1.justification: The GPT-5 response-generation procedure and proxy-evaluation prompts in A.2–A.3 are unchanged. Privacy-conscious personas and few-shot prompting are suggested as future work, not implemented method components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 90 PrivacyLens scenarios and seven helpfulness/privacy questions using 94 U.S.-based, English-fluent participants. The expanded cultural discussion introduces no evaluation of additional populations or tasks.

E2.justification: The same five proxy models—Gemma-3, GPT-5, Llama-3.3, Mistral, and Qwen-3—participate in the corresponding human–LLM and cross-model comparisons in Tables 1, 3, and 4.

E3.justification: The sampling design, 470 participant ratings, eligibility, prompts, and evaluation metrics are retained. V4's explicit temperatures, role instructions, and intermediate Likert values document previously described settings rather than establish a revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Sections 3.1 and 3.3 newly report inspections for distinctive GPT-5 writing styles and participant misunderstanding of survey questions, finding no clear evidence of either. Existing scenario case studies and variability analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five independent evaluations per proxy LLM and retain the same dispersion reporting and Table 3 significance convention, p < 0.001. No new seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Section 4.1 corrects disagreement on personal privacy preferences from 95% to 96% of scenarios, specifying 86/90 in v4. V4 also newly reports the negative findings from its style and comprehension checks. The main agreement, correlation, similarity values, and plotted distributions are retained.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces original theorems or proofs. The contextual-integrity framework and statistical definitions are retained; explicitly listing intermediate values in the existing evenly spaced Likert coding adds explanation without changing the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, three research questions, and central claims about proxy–human misalignment remain unchanged. The Introduction adds the broader implication that proxy-based evaluations may misrepresent actual user risks.

C2.justification: V4 explains the rationale and scope of direct role prompting, proposes personas and few-shot human rationales as possible remedies, and expands the existing U.S.-sample limitation into a discussion of cultural generalizability. These extensions remain untested suggestions and qualifications.

D1.justification: Reproducibility documentation expands substantially: A.6 supplies the qualitative codebook, Table 2 specifies four models' temperatures, and A.4 replaces a future-release promise with an artifact link advertised as providing anonymized evaluations, proxy judgments, and an analysis script. The PDFs establish the access disclosure, not the linked contents.

R1.justification: V4 adds Fabbri et al. (2021) for sampling rationale and Herbert et al. (2025), Munyendo (2026), and Naveed et al. (2022) for cultural context, while removing Pan et al. (2024). The Zhang citation consolidation concerns the same arXiv work, not removal of a distinct research contribution.

P1.justification: V4 makes localized Methods and Discussion expansions, prose and reference-format edits, adds acknowledgments and the codebook section, and changes author order and email presentation. The main section sequence and research-question structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 changes panel proportions and annotation sizing and suppresses some percentage labels while retaining its distributions. Table 2 gains a temperature column, Table 1 shifts relative to Figure 2, and appendix plots are rearranged. Other graphical content is retained.

improvement.justification: V4 improves transparency through the codebook, explicit temperatures, and artifact access instructions, while clarifying study choices and generalizability and correcting a result summary. The central empirical evidence is retained. The new checks remain qualitative, and the added actual-risk implication extends beyond measured perceptions, so the overall gain is limited.
